title: Operation Bretagne ends, with French victory over the Viet Minh in Vietnam.
text: Operation Bretagne was a French Union military operation between 1 December 1952 and 4 January 1953, during the First Indochina War. Four Mobile Groups and General de Berchoux's two Amphibian Sub-Groups hunted and engaged the 9th Regiment (304th Division) and the 48th Regiment (320th Division) of the Viet Minh, who were threatening the bishopric of Bui Chu, in Nam Định province.

title: France agrees to the provisional independence of Cambodia with the king Norodom Sihanouk.
text: Norodom Sihanouk was King, Chief of State and Prime Minister of Cambodia. He is known as Samdech Euv (meaning "King Father") or by his nickname The Pink Prince.

title: First meeting of the assembly of the European Economic Community in Strasbourg.
text: Strasbourg is a prefecture and commune, and the largest city of the Grand Est region of northeastern France, in the historic region of Alsace. It is the prefecture of the Bas-Rhin department and the official seat of the European Parliament.

title: Miss France Christiane Martel Won Miss Universe 1953
text: Christiane Martel is a French-Mexican actress, model and beauty queen. She became the second woman to win the Miss Universe beauty pageant in 1953.

title: Operation Camargue, further French military action against the Viet Minh, begins.
text: Operation Camargue was one of the largest operations by the French Far East Expeditionary Corps and Vietnamese National Army in the First Indochina War. It took place from 28 July until 10 August 1953.

title: General strike ends in France.
text: A general strike is a strike action in which a substantial proportion of the total labour force in a city, region, or country participates. General strikes are characterised by the participation of workers from a multitude of workplaces across different industries, and tend to involve entire communities.

title: Cambodia becomes independent from France.
text: Independence is a condition of a nation, country, or state, in which residents and population, or some portion thereof, exercise self-government, and usually sovereignty, over its territory. The opposite of independence is the status of a dependent territory or colony.

title: Operation Castor, airborne operation to establish a fortified airhead in Điện Biên Province, starts.
text: Operation Castor was a successful airborne operation for French Union forces in the First Indochina War. This operation of France and the State of Vietnam established a fortified airhead in Điện Biên Province against the communist Việt Minh, in the north-west corner of Vietnam and was commanded by Brigadier General Jean Gilles.

title: Tour de France begins.
text: The 1953 Tour de France was the 40th edition of the Tour de France, taking place from 3 to 26 July. It consisted of 22 stages over 4,476 km.

title: Tour de France ends, won by Louison Bobet.
text: Louis "Louison" Bobet was a French professional road racing cyclist. He was the first great French rider of the post-war period and the first rider to win the Tour de France in three successive years, from 1953 to 1955.

title: En Attendant Godot premiered at Théâtre de Babylone
text: Waiting for Godot is a play by Irish playwright and author Samuel Beckett. It was written, first published (1952), and first performed (1953) in French as En attendant Godot.
